questions.q:
Will Leidos Holdings, Inc. (LDOS) have a higher rate of return than Marvell Technology, Inc. (MRVL) between {forecast_due_date} and {resolution_date}?

For each resolution date, a stock's rate of return is calculated as its market close price on that date divided by its market close price on {forecast_due_date}, minus one. Prices are adjusted for stock splits and reverse splits. Dividends are not included. If either stock is delisted (e.g., through acquisition, merger, or bankruptcy), the most recent market close price before delisting is used for all subsequent resolution dates. | horizon 2026-11-01
questions.resolution_note: Resolves using the market close prices at https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/LDOS and https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MRVL. If a date in the question coincides with a day the market is closed (weekend, holiday, etc.) the previous market close price is used.

base_rate_used.reference_class: relative stock-pair performance, near-efficient random walk

evidence: Dataset family 'yfinance', horizon 2026-11-01: base 0.50 with 30-day momentum tilt -0.04 from freeze changes ['-7.8', '+21.8'].
questions.strongest_opposing_case: Strongest case against: the family rule ignores series-specific news and regime changes; any structural break since the freeze date (war shocks, policy moves, product relists) would move the true probability well away from this base rate.
